The generalized Gamma distribution for SAR intensities

Source: R/distributions-intensity.R
dggamma.Rd

Density, distribution function, quantile function and random generation for the generalized Gamma (Stacy) law with power \(\alpha > 0\), shape \(\phi > 0\) and inverse-scale \(\mu > 0\): $$f(z) = \frac{\alpha \mu^{\alpha\phi}}{\Gamma(\phi)} z^{\alpha\phi - 1} \exp\{-(\mu z)^\alpha\}, \quad z > 0.$$ For \(\alpha = 1\) it reduces to the Gamma law with shape \(\phi\) and rate \(\mu\); in SAR applications \(\phi\) plays the role of the number of looks.

Usage

dggamma(x, alpha, phi, mu, log = FALSE)

pggamma(q, alpha, phi, mu, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)

qggamma(p, alpha, phi, mu, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)

rggamma(n, alpha, phi, mu)

Arguments

x, q

Vector of quantiles.

alpha

Power parameter (\(\alpha > 0\)).

phi

Shape parameter (\(\phi > 0\)).

mu

Inverse-scale parameter (\(\mu > 0\)).

log, log.p

Logical; if TRUE, probabilities/densities are given as logarithms.

lower.tail

Logical; if TRUE (default) probabilities are \(P(X \le x)\), otherwise \(P(X > x)\).

p

Vector of probabilities.

n

Number of observations.

Value

Density, distribution function, quantile function or random deviates.

References

Li, H.-C., Hong, W., Wu, Y.-R. and Fan, P.-Z. (2011). On the empirical- statistical modeling of SAR images with generalized gamma distribution. IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Signal Processing, 5(3), 386–397.

See also

GGammaSAR for the R6 interface.

Examples

dggamma(c(0.5, 1, 2), alpha = 1.5, phi = 2, mu = 1)
#> [1] 0.2633207 0.5518192 0.3546345
rggamma(3, alpha = 1.5, phi = 2, mu = 1)
#> [1] 2.148747 1.881254 1.194354
